builds.howItPlays: You spend Energy to summon a ready Sprite token that fights immediately, and the more Sprites you already have out the cheaper the next one gets. You throw these disposable units into fights to trade with your opponent's real units, then push your permanent units through to take the battlefields those trades open up.
builds.whyYou: You like getting the most out of units you know won't stick around, treating each Sprite as a trade you're happy to make. You enjoy timing when to send a token in and when to pull it back before it expires, and you don't mind a bit of bookkeeping if it means getting more out of every turn than your opponent does. If you'd rather out-maneuver your opponent piece by piece than overpower them outright, Lillia is a good fit.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 4: riftbound.gg describes 'a mid-paced, value-focused strategy' that forces trades rather than racing, and notes the deck 'lacks a decisive finisher', so it sits in the midgame band rather than a fast or a truly slow one. stance 5: hextechanalytics calls it 'a fast, proactive tempo' deck early, throwing Sprites out immediately, but riftbound.gg says it 'has been forced to adapt to the metagame, with more support spells and gear removal', pulling the average toward the middle of the scale. complexity 7: hextechanalytics warns 'counting every token as an immediate attacker overstates the turn', requiring you to track Temporary-unit expiry, readiness, and positioning around the Hold phase all at once. variance 3.5: riftbound.gg calls the deck 'a fairly obvious deck to build, but not a very flexible one', and hextechanalytics frames it as trading disposable units in a fairly linear way, so outcomes are more consistent than swingy. Ability: pay Energy 4 and exhaust to play a ready 3 Might Sprite unit token with Temporary, costing 1 less Energy for each friendly Temporary unit you already control. Confidence: medium; the seed guessed Combo, but neither guide describes an assembled combo finish, both call the deck value/token-trading with 'no decisive finisher', which is why this draft reclassifies it to Midrange. Reviewer should double check that reclassification.
